generator.earthplatform.earth.info: The real Earth at true scale and height
earthplatform.setup.title: Where on Earth do you want to start?
earthplatform.setup.hint: Pick a famous place, search for any town on the globe, or type any latitude and longitude. You can travel anywhere later with /earth.
earthplatform.setup.globe.tooltip: Spin and zoom a globe of the real Earth, then click where you want to begin.
earthplatform.setup.imagery.tooltip: Color the ground from satellite photos (EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery, downloaded like the terrain). Applies to new worlds and is saved in the Earth settings.
earthplatform.setup.invalid: Latitude must be between -80 and 80, longitude between -180 and 180.
earthplatform.arrival.title: Preparing your Earth
earthplatform.arrival.downloading: Downloading terrain, land cover and climate%s
earthplatform.arrival.firstVisit: This only happens the first time you visit a place. Everything is kept on your computer afterwards.
earthplatform.arrival.slow: This is taking a while. The data servers may be slow; it will keep trying.
earthplatform.arrival.unreachable: Can't reach the Earth data servers
earthplatform.arrival.unreachable.hint: Check your internet connection. Earth Platform needs it the first time you visit a place; we'll keep trying and you'll arrive as soon as it works.
earthplatform.arrival.offlineMode: Offline mode is on, and this place isn't downloaded yet
earthplatform.arrival.offlineMode.hint: Turn off offline mode in Mods > Earth Platform > Config, then restart the game, so this place can be downloaded.
earthplatform.status.unreachable: Can't reach the Earth data servers
earthplatform.status.unreachable.hint: Places you've visited still work. New ground fills in when you're back online.
earthplatform.configuration.title: Earth Settings
earthplatform.configuration.farTerrain.t: How the land beyond your render distance looks
earthplatform.configuration.farDetail.to: How far the far terrain reaches, in steps of about 8 km: 4 = 37 km, 11 = 94 km (default), 24 = 201 km (125 mi). 25 to 48 (up to 397 km, 247 mi) is the extreme range, for very powerful computers. Farther uses more memory and takes longer to fill in. Changes at once, no restart. Also on the pause menu in Earth worlds, in km and miles.
earthplatform.configuration.farSharpness: How sharp far terrain looks: how close coarser levels take over. Sharper keeps finer detail further out but takes longer to fill in and uses more memory. Fast fills in quickest. Extreme and Ultra are for very powerful computers: they cost several times as much as Balanced and can drop to single-digit frame rates even on fast ones, Ultra most of all. Changes at once, no restart. Also on the pause menu in Earth worlds.
earthplatform.pause.distance.tooltip: How far the far terrain reaches, from 37 to 201 km, and up to 397 km in the extreme range for very powerful computers. Farther uses more memory and takes longer to fill in. Changes when you let go of the slider, no restart.
earthplatform.pause.sharpness.tooltip: Far terrain sharpness. Sharper keeps finer detail further out but takes longer to fill in and uses more memory. Fast fills in quickest. Extreme and Ultra are for very powerful computers and can drop to single-digit frame rates even on fast ones, Ultra most of all. Changes at once.
earthplatform.configuration.farTargetFps: A frame rate to hold, or 0 for off (the default). When set, far terrain sharpness steps down a choice at a time, no lower than Fast, while the game runs slower than this, and comes back up to the sharpness you chose when there is room again. It never goes sharper than your choice and leaves the far distance alone.
earthplatform.stretch.true: Land there is drawn true to size.
earthplatform.stretch.there: Land there is drawn %s× as wide as in life; heights are real.
earthplatform.stretch.home: True to size here. Land is %s× as wide at the equator, %s× at %s°.
earthplatform.configuration.farTexturedL: How many far levels are drawn with block textures; further ones use flat colors. Default 8, all of them.
earthplatform.configuration.showDownload: A small note while Earth data downloads, and a warning when it can't be reached.
earthplatform.configuration.preselectEar: Choose the Earth world type when you open Create World.
How high clouds float in Earth worlds, in meters above sea level. They also stay at least 1200 m over the ground you stand on, so mountains and plateaus get a sky too. 0 keeps vanilla clouds at Y 192. Shader packs draw their own clouds. Default 2500.
earthplatform.configuration.layeredCloud: Three thick cloud banks at different heights, each with its own wind, and weather that clears and clouds over, instead of the single deck. Without a shader pack only. They can still cut into mountains, and the high bank can show straight streaks.
earthplatform.configuration.cloudQuality: How finely the layered clouds are sampled. Higher costs GPU time.
earthplatform.configuration.cloudOpacity: The most the layered clouds may hide, so some of the view stays when flying inside a bank. Default 0.72.
earthplatform.configuration.group.farTer: Looks and features of the land beyond your render distance
earthplatform.configuration.group.flying: What the game does when you fly or climb high
earthplatform.configuration.group.sky.to: Clouds beyond the layered cloud settings above
earthplatform.configuration.group.nearby: How blocks around you are loaded, culled and drawn
earthplatform.configuration.group.compat: Switches for shader packs and for graphics cards that need them
earthplatform.configuration.group.speedu: Faster ways of doing the same work, and the older ways to compare them with. None should change what you see or the blocks made. Switch one only to compare
earthplatform.configuration.group.diagno: Checks, logs and timers for testing. Most slow the game down
earthplatform.configuration.group.worldD: Which data new worlds are made from. Existing worlds keep what they were made with
earthplatform.configuration.farSmooth.to: Draws far ground smooth instead of blocky, trees included. The four finest levels, which show your edits, keep their blocks, and so does a column with near cubes drawn within its height. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farBlockText: Far textures keep one block's size at every level instead of half a voxel's, fade to their average color as they shrink to a few pixels, and coarse voxels are lit by their slope. Not tried under a shader pack. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farFade.tool: Far levels fade into each other. Off, they meet at a visible seam. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farZoom.tool: A zoomed view (spyglass, zoom mod) asks for sharper far terrain where it looks. Off keeps the far levels round the player alone. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCurvature: Far terrain, its water and the layered clouds drop away with the Earth's curve as the camera climbs from 1,500 to 6,000 blocks above the ground, for the eye only; the world, collisions and saves stay flat. Without a shader pack only. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farAtmospher: From 2,000 to 6,000 blocks above the ground, far terrain hazes with its distance and its textures fade to their average color past half a kilometer. Without a shader pack only. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCruiseSmo: Needs Smooth far ground on and a first smooth level past 5, which only the command line sets (-Dearthplatform.far.smoothFrom): while the camera is over 2,200 blocks above the ground, smoothing reaches down to level 5. Does nothing otherwise, or under a shader pack. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farPlainDept: Precise far depth for layered clouds

While the layered clouds draw, without a shader pack, far terrain draws in its own 32-bit depth so the clouds meet distant mountains cleanly. Off leaves it in the game's coarse depth. Does nothing with layered clouds off. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesCaveCul: Leaves out near cubes that lie behind rock from the camera, as vanilla does for its sections. Off draws every cube in view. The shadow map still draws them. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesCaveLin: With cave culling, past 60 blocks a step into the next cube is also taken only where the line back to the camera runs through cubes the search reached, as vanilla does. Off leaves that look out. Does nothing with cave culling off. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesOcclusi: Leaves out near cubes hidden behind others, tested on the GPU with OpenGL 3.3 occlusion queries (a Mac too). Off by default: on a GeForce RTX 2080 Ti under Photon the tests cost more than they saved. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesShadowC: Under a shader pack, near cubes go into the shadow map through Iris's own shadow frustum, leaving out what can cast no shadow into the view where the pack allows. Off culls by the map's box only. Shader packs only. Restart the game to apply.
With cave culling and shadow culling, where the camera is shut in, the shadow map takes only the cubes whose shadow can reach what the cave search found. Shader packs only. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesSkipInt: Meshing a near cube skips a cube of solid stone or deepslate sealed in by more of it on all six faces, below its column's sky: it is neither lit nor walked over. The same light and vertices. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesReuseSn: A near cube's blocks are copied once for all the mesh snapshots it is in (up to 27), kept for the last 1,024 cubes, instead of once for each. The same blocks. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farLodDepth: Far terrain's own depth under shader packs
Under a shader pack, far terrain keeps a depth buffer of its own. Off makes it share the game's depth buffer. Shader packs only. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farDhPacks: Shader packs made for Distant Horizons
earthplatform.configuration.farDhPacks.t: Under a shader pack that has a Distant Horizons terrain program (dh_terrain) and no Voxy code, far terrain draws with that program. Off leaves such packs with far terrain in plain colors. Not used when Distant Horizons is installed. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farHiddenCul: Hide far faces behind far terrain
With the depth pre-pass, leaves out far faces that lie wholly behind other far terrain, tested on the GPU. OpenGL 4.3 only, so never on a Mac. The same pixels. Restart the game to apply.
With hiding of far faces (OpenGL 4.3 only), the depth pre-pass draws first the ranges the last frame's test showed, then only those they don't hide. Off by default: under Photon at Yosemite it left far cliffs hatched with holes. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farQueryCull: Where far terrain draws in one pass (a Mac, no shader pack, or a pack without Voxy support), leaves out far ranges hidden behind terrain already drawn, using OpenGL 3.3 occlusion queries. Off by default: it was slower on the one card measured, and is not yet measured on a Mac. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farSkipNear: Skip far columns inside the near cubes
Under a shader pack with Voxy support, leaves out of the far pass the columns that lie wholly inside the game's blocks' reach, where it draws no pixel of them anyway. Off draws them, for comparing. Shader packs with Voxy support only. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farReplayPre: With the depth pre-pass (shader packs with Voxy support), the shading pass draws the ranges the pre-pass drew instead of queueing every column again. Off queues them again, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farFirstMesh: Far columns never meshed go ahead of remeshes, real ones first. Off, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farMeshQueue: Far mesher queue grows with frame time
The far meshers' queue grows with the frame time. Off keeps it at 128, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farFastWater: Off restores full water scans and uniform updates, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farTrackByte: Track far memory as it changes
Off sums every far column for each memory query, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCachePick: Keep the far pick between frames
Off rebuilds selection, sorting and face groups every frame, for comparing. Also turns off the kept far walk and the switches that build on it. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farSharedWat: Keeps every far column's water in one vertex buffer per format, so each water pass binds it once. Off gives each column its own again, for comparing. The same triangles. Also turns off batched far water. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farBatchWate: With shared far water buffers, draws all the columns in a 16,384-block cube with one multi-draw. Off draws each column on its own, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farBatchStam: Upload far fade stamps in batches
Uploads the fade stamps selection writes once it ends, adjacent slots in one call. Off uploads each as it is written, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farNearGroun: Keep far terrain off the ground you stand on

While the ground near you loads, far terrain inside the game's blocks' reach draws only where those blocks drew nothing, so coarse far voxels no longer cover the blocks at your feet. Off always draws it as before. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farLinkColum: Link far columns to their finer ones

Each far column keeps links to the columns a level finer under and beside it, so selection needs no hash lookup per step. Off looks each up, for comparing. The same selection. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farReuseDraw: While the far pick stands, each far pass draws again the ranges it queued the frame before. Off queues them every frame, for comparing. The same draws. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farViewMargi: Hold the far view while the camera barely moves

The far view takes in every column it would from anywhere within 16 blocks of the camera, and holds while the camera stays inside that. Off works the view out whenever the camera moves or turns, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farReuseWalk: Keeps the walk of the far pyramid (which columns draw) while the camera stays in the same level 2 column. Off walks it whenever the view changes, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farQuietMesh: Walk again only when a mesh matters
With the kept walk, a mesh that does not change what the walk draws no longer causes a new walk. Off walks again for every such mesh, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCoarseWal: With the kept walk, while the finest far level drawn is a coarser one (high up or very fast), the walk waits for a column of the level above the finest. Off walks at every level 2 column, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farSentInPla: Swap resent far columns in place
With the kept walk, a column the server sends again takes the old one's place in the walk instead of walking the pyramid again. Off walks again, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farPartialWa: Walk only the branches that changed
With quiet meshes, a walk due only for columns meshed or fades ended walks just the branches they change. Off walks all of it, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farMovePatch: Patch the walk as the camera moves
With partial walks, the camera entering another column walks again just the branches that change with it. Off walks all of it, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farMaskChang: Update the far mask from the last one
Each far mask (which near cubes each far column leaves out) starts from the last one. Off works every column's cubes out afresh each time, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farReuseOrde: Each view of the far columns puts them in order starting from the last view's. Off sorts them afresh every frame, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farIndexed.t: Off draws six corners per face instead of indexed faces. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farIndexedAl: Find far GPU space by size
Off scans free ranges by address, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farSplitRang: Draw every far group as its own range
On draws every far group as its own range, for comparing. Slower; leave it off. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCacheCove: Work out near-cube cover once per far column
Off looks the cover up per block, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farRunMesher: Mesh plain far columns from runs

Meshes plain far columns (level 3 and coarser, one biome, no near cubes) from vertical runs of blocks, with the same faces. Off always uses the block-by-block mesher, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farRecentLoo: Each far mesher thread remembers the last few hundred looks it was given for a block, side and biome. Off asks the shared table for every face, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCullTree: Test far columns through a tree
Drawn far columns are tested against the view through a tree. Off tests every column on its own, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesSkipBur: Meshing a near cube leaves out, before the model pass, blocks whose six faces vanilla's face check hides and whose model is one of vanilla's plain kinds. Off sends every block through, for comparing. The same vertices. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesReusePo: Meshing a near cube draws each block with one pose set to its place. Off pushes a copy for every block, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesOcclusi: With occlusion culling of near cubes, tests only the box sides that face the camera: the same answer for half the fill. Off draws both sides. Does nothing with occlusion culling off. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesRegions: Share near-cube vertex buffers by region

Near cube meshes share vertex buffers by region (8 cubes a side) and each opaque layer draws with one multi-draw, using about 1.4 times the meshes' own bytes. Off gives every cube its own buffers, as before. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubicLightma: Upload the lightmap to three textures in turn
In cubic worlds without a shader pack, so an upload never waits on frames still drawing with the last one. Off always uploads to one texture, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCheckWalk: Also walks the far pyramid afresh every frame and logs a warning naming the columns whenever the kept walk would draw different ones. For testing; slow. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCheckMask: Also works every far column's cubes out afresh after each mask and logs a warning naming any column whose cubes differ. For testing; slow. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesCheckMe: Also meshes and lights every near cube the plain way and logs a warning naming any cube whose light or vertices differ. For testing; slow. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farGpuTimers: Times far terrain GPU passes with OpenGL queries and adds them to the performance log. Off for players because the queries wrap other mods' and shader packs' draws. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farQueryCull: Logs the counts of far occlusion queries every 20 frames. Does nothing unless far occlusion queries are on. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubicPerf.to: Logs every timing every few seconds. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.perfLog.tool: Writes a small local performance log (frame times, GPU and driver, graphics settings, terrain workload; no names, places or paths) to earthplatform/perf in the game folder. Off writes nothing. Restart the game to apply.
New worlds shape trees from the canopy height map. Off lets trees take any of their kind's shapes, and giant sequoias stand only in the Sierra Nevada's listed groves. Applies to worlds you make after changing it.
earthplatform.configuration.earthMaps: Rock, red ground and soil maps
earthplatform.configuration.earthMaps.to: New worlds use the bundled rock, red ground and soil maps. Off falls back to boxes of latitude and longitude for red deserts and lava fields. Applies to worlds you make after changing it.
New worlds place cacti, bamboo and cherries by ecoregion realm and climate. Off uses boxes of latitude and longitude. Applies to worlds you make after changing it.
The server makes quick stand-ins for far columns and sends them first; the client shows them until the real columns arrive. Off on a server makes none; off on a client asks for none, so far terrain comes in without them. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubicFlightS: Server setting. A player flying 48 or more blocks over the ground keeps getting the real ground and water out to the cube view distance (192 blocks at most) and within 384 blocks in a straight line. Not load-tested with many players. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.viewOrder: Load what you look at first
earthplatform.configuration.viewOrder.to: Server setting, also read by the client. Near cubes load by what the player looks at first. Off loads them by distance alone. Restart the game to apply.
Server setting. Makes every buried cube instead of skipping rock out of sight. Slower; for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.riversFastSa: Off restores the allocating per-pixel strength sampler and per-cell nearby maxima lookups, for comparing. The same output. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cogsFastRead: Fast reading of national elevation files
Off restores per-pixel block lookups and per-pixel overview shapes when 3DEP, REMA and HRDEM files are read, for comparing. The same values. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.climateRowCh: Keeps CHELSA climate rows in memory as 2048-column chunks. Off keeps them whole, which decodes whole rows far more often. The same values. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.copernicusFa: Off makes the Copernicus fill ask the shared caches for each tile pixel's check size and part, for comparing. The same weights. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.earthEveryLa: Lay every elevation layer over every tile
On lays every elevation layer over every tile, as before, also where a later layer replaces a tile whole. The same tiles; for comparing how long a trip waits. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesFastBlo: Off restores per-block sphere sums for ore and rock blobs, for comparing. The cubes are identical. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesPlainRa: Draws each cube's veins, cave plants and structure plans, and the random numbers meshing asks for, from a plain random source. Off uses vanilla's legacy source, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubesFastLig: Lights a cube's 48-block neighborhood filling cubes of one state at once. Off goes over every block, for comparing. The same light. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farFastReach: Off restores the shrinking flood queue and per-sample land cover lookups in the water reach windows, for comparing. The same output. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farFastDrown: Columns ask the water reach windows for reservoirs only where one can be found. Off asks for every column near a reservoir-sized patch of water, for comparing. The same output. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farGiveWay: Let stand-ins have half the processors
earthplatform.configuration.farGiveWay.t: Real far columns leave up to half their processors to stand-ins being made. Off, for comparing. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farSurfacePa: Send plain far columns as runs
Far columns that are only ground, water and cover are made, sent and kept on disk as vertical runs. Off sends every column as sections, as before build 70. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.earthPrepare: Log what a place's data waited on
After each fetch of a place's data, logs which pieces came in last and how long each took. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.farCheckPack: Also makes each column of runs as sections and compares; one that differs is logged and sent as sections. Doubles the work of making far columns. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.configuration.cubicTrace.t: Logs cubes sent and received. Restart the game to apply.
earthplatform.sodium.allSettings.tooltip: Opens every Earth Platform setting, including world and server ones such as travel, homes, satellite imagery and the download cache.
Where new Earth worlds start when nobody picked a place, for example on a server: a famous place id from /earth places, or "latitude,longitude".
earthplatform.configuration.offline.tool: Never download Earth data; only places already downloaded generate.
earthplatform.configuration.cacheLimit.t: Largest size of the downloaded Earth data. The least recently used files are removed when the game starts. 0 keeps everything.
earthplatform.configuration.satelliteIma: Color the ground of new Earth worlds from satellite photos (EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery, downloaded like the terrain). Existing worlds keep what they were made with.
earthplatform.configuration.anyoneCanTra: Everyone can use /earth visit and goto
When off, only operators can travel with commands. The singleplayer owner always can.
earthplatform.configuration.anyoneCanUse: Everyone can use /earth home and spawn
Lets every player save a home with /earth sethome, go back to it, and go to the server spawn.
earthplatform.configuration.playersChoos: Each new player can pick, once, where they start on a globe. They respawn there when they have no bed.
earthplatform.configuration.teleportRequ: Players can ask to teleport to each other with /earth tpa and /earth tpahere.
earthplatform.configuration.showPlayersO: Other players show as green dots on the travel map.
earthplatform.configuration.countryNames: Shows "Now entering..." when you cross into another country.
earthplatform.configuration.travelLevels: Experience levels a survival player pays for a trip by command. 0 is free.
earthplatform.configuration.travelCooldo: How long a survival player waits between trips by command.
earthplatform.configuration.dailyRace.to: Starts a race to a random famous place each day.
earthplatform.configuration.raceReward.t: An item and a count, such as minecraft:diamond 5.
earthplatform.configuration.webMapPort.t: The port the web map listens on.
earthplatform.configuration.webMapAddres: Where the web map answers: 0.0.0.0 for every network, 127.0.0.1 for this computer only, or one of the server's own IP addresses.
earthplatform.configuration.warps.toolti: Lets players go to the server's warps with /earth warp.
Lets players go somewhere random on land with /earth random.
earthplatform.configuration.whereOnEarth: Lets operators start Where on Earth guessing rounds with /earth guess start.
earthplatform.configuration.races.toolti: Lets operators start races to famous places with /earth race start.
earthplatform.configuration.webMap.toolt: Serves a live map of the players in a web browser, on the web map port.
Players who can't use the travel map can still open the map (N) to look around and point a compass at a spot, a famous place, their home or another player. It never moves anyone.
earthplatform.globe.title: Choose where your Earth begins
earthplatform.globe.hint: Click the globe to choose a spot.
earthplatform.globe.polar: Worlds can start between 80°S and 80°N. Pick somewhere a little closer to the equator.
earthplatform.globe.credit: NASA Blue Marble, AWS Terrain Tiles, ESA WorldCover
earthplatform.globe.offline: Offline: showing the built-in map only
earthplatform.globe.controls: Drag to spin, scroll to zoom, click to place the pin
earthplatform.map.title: Where to?
earthplatform.map.hint: Click the globe where you want to go. The blue dot is you.
earthplatform.map.creativeOnly: The travel map is for creative mode.
earthplatform.map.spawn.title: Choose the server spawn
earthplatform.map.spawn.hint: Click the globe where new players should arrive. The blue dot is you.
earthplatform.map.start.title: Choose where you start
earthplatform.map.start.hint: Click the globe where you want to begin. You can choose once.
earthplatform.map.guess.title: Where are you?
earthplatform.map.guess.hint: Click the globe where you think you are.
earthplatform.map.look.title: Map
earthplatform.map.look.hint: Click a spot or a player to point your compass there. The blue dot is you.
earthplatform.map.look.noCompass: Carry a compass to point it somewhere. The blue dot is you.
item.earthplatform.compass.follows: Follows %s while they're on the Earth
earthplatform.postcard.saved: Postcard saved as %s. Place code %s: anyone can come here with /earth code.
earthplatform.postcard.failed: The postcard could not be saved: %s
